blocks.content: Delhi's economy chapter is dominated by its status as a services-driven, high-per-capita-income capital city economy - distinct from most Indian states which retain a larger agricultural or manufacturing base.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Indian economy is structured into Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors, each contributing uniquely to national output and employment.
The Tertiary (Services) sector is the largest driver of Gross Value Added (GVA) in India.
The Primary sector (Agriculture & Allied) continues to absorb the highest proportion of the workforce.
Robust connectivity and infrastructure projects, such as PM Gati Shakti, are essential for seamless economic integration.

blocks.content: Delhi's economy is overwhelmingly dominated by the tertiary (services) sector - trade, finance, real estate, public administration, IT/ITeS, education and healthcare - given its role as both national capital and a major commercial/trading hub of north India.

Agriculture forms a negligible share of Delhi's economy owing to its small, heavily urbanised land area; whatever agricultural activity remains is concentrated in peripheral rural pockets, primarily vegetable and dairy farming for the city's own consumption.

Delhi has consistently ranked among the highest Indian states/UTs by per-capita income (Net State Domestic Product per capita), reflecting its concentration of high-value service-sector jobs, government employment, and corporate/trading activity.

cells: Tertiary/services - trade, finance, real estate, public administration, IT/ITeS
Negligible; concentrated in peripheral rural pockets (vegetables, dairy)
Consistently among the highest of all Indian states/UTs
Chandni Chowk (wholesale/traditional trade), Karol Bagh, Sadar Bazar, Khari Baoli (Asia's largest spice market), Connaught Place (commercial/retail hub)
Okhla Industrial Area, Naraina, Wazirpur (small-scale manufacturing); Aerocity and Dwarka (services/hospitality hubs near the airport)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Khari Baoli in Old Delhi is frequently cited as 'Asia's largest wholesale spice market' - a specific, commonly tested economic-geography one-liner.

items: Exams frequently contrast the employment share vs. GVA contribution of the Primary and Services sectors.
Key flagship schemes like Bharatmala, Sagarmala, and PM Gati Shakti are critical topics for infrastructure questions.
Understand the conceptual difference between Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and Gross Value Added (GVA).
Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), Delhi - one of India's busiest airports and a major international aviation hub, located in the Palam/Dwarka area of south-west Delhi.

Delhi Metro - one of the world's largest and busiest urban metro rail networks, operated by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), a landmark public transport project since its first line opened in 2002, now spanning multiple lines across Delhi-NCR.
Delhi is a major rail junction on the Indian Railways network, served principally by New Delhi Railway Station, Old Delhi Railway Station, Hazrat Nizamuddin, and Anand Vihar terminals.

As the National Capital, Delhi hosts the headquarters of most central government ministries, PSUs, and a dense concentration of embassies/diplomatic missions (chiefly in the Chanakyapuri diplomatic enclave), making government administration itself a major driver of the local economy.
Delhi's economy is services-dominated; among the highest per-capita income UTs/states in India.
Khari Baoli, Old Delhi - reputed to be Asia's largest wholesale spice market.
Indira Gandhi International Airport and the Delhi Metro (DMRC, since 2002) are flagship infrastructure assets.
Chanakyapuri is Delhi's principal diplomatic enclave, housing most foreign embassies.
